aboutH2: Field Trip Health Toronto: Revolutionizing Mental Health Treatment
intro: Field Trip Health Toronto is a forward-thinking mental health clinic that offers medication-assisted therapy (MAT) to individuals struggling with severe depression, anxiety, and PTSD. With a team of experienced medical and mental health experts, the clinic provides the highest quality of care by using evidence-based treatments to address the underlying causes of mental illness.

The Toronto clinic is an outpatient service. You come in for scheduled appointments on weekdays and go home the same day, and there are no beds or overnight stays. Since Field Trip's 2023 restructuring, the Canadian clinics have been run under the name Field Trip Health Canada, and the Toronto location is still open at 30 Duncan Street with its own medical and therapy team.

pillars.title: Medication-assisted Treatment (MAT)
pillars.body: MAT is a revolutionary approach to treating mental health disorders that involves using medications that work in conjunction with therapy to alleviate symptoms. Field Trip Health Toronto uses ketamine-assisted therapy, a form of MAT that has been shown to be highly effective in treating treatment-resistant depression and anxiety. The therapy involves administering a low dose of ketamine to the patient, which stimulates the growth of new neural connections in the brain. The patient is then guided through a talk therapy session that helps them process their emotions and develop coping strategies.

pillars.title: Personalized Treatment Plans
pillars.body: At Field Trip Health Toronto, each patient receives a personalized treatment plan tailored to their unique needs and preferences. The clinic’s highly trained therapists work with patients to identify their goals and develop an individualized therapy plan that works for them. The clinic uses a variety of evidence-based therapies, including cognitive behavioral therapy, somatic experience, and dance movement therapy, to help patients achieve long-term wellness.

pillars.title: Spa-like Therapeutic Space
pillars.body: Field Trip Health Toronto’s clinic is designed to be a calming, spa-like environment that supports the healing process. In addition to offering cutting-edge therapies, the clinic provides several ancillary services to enhance patients’ wellness journey. These include dietician services, yoga classes, and massage therapy, all of which are trauma-informed and designed to support patients’ physical and emotional well-being.

overviewH2: Field Trip Health Toronto: Center Overview
overview: Field Trip Health is a rehab center that specializes in providing safe and legal ketamine-assisted therapy to individuals struggling with treatment-resistant mental health conditions. With a team of medical and mental health professionals, Field Trip offers evidence-based and medically-supervised psychedelic-assisted therapies to clients in Toronto seeking relief from conditions such as depression, anxiety, and PTSD.

Field Trip’s ketamine-assisted therapy combines ketamine therapy with follow-up talk therapy sessions to provide holistic treatment to clients. The rehab center’s Toronto Health Center is designed to be a comfortable and healing space, with calming spa-like areas and expert professionals on hand to provide support throughout the healing journey. Field Trip’s approach to psychological and psychiatric care is cutting-edge, research-based, and dedicated to delivering the highest standard of care to clients.

faqIntro: Answers come from the clinic's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Field Trip Health Toronto a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. It is an outpatient day clinic in downtown Toronto, open on weekdays, and you go home after each appointment. There are no beds, overnight stays or detox. If you need live-in treatment or medically supervised withdrawal, ask the care team on your discovery call, or compare residential centres in the GTA and across Ontario.

faqs.q: Is the Toronto clinic still open, and who runs it?
faqs.a: Yes. The clinic at 30 Duncan Street, Suite 400 is open and taking bookings in October 2026, under the name Field Trip Health Canada. The original Field Trip Health company went through a court-supervised restructuring in 2023, and its Canadian clinics were bought by the Canadian Centre for Psychedelic Healing. The old fieldtriphealth.com site now covers US clinics only, so use fieldtriphealth.ca for Toronto.

faqs.q: How much does ketamine-assisted therapy cost at Field Trip Health Toronto? Can I use my benefits?
faqs.a: The clinic does not publish prices; costs depend on how the medicine is given and how many sessions your plan includes, and the team explains them on a free discovery call. The 50-minute nurse practitioner consultation has a fee because OHIP does not cover it. Public plans don't pay for the medication or medical parts, but many clients claim the psychotherapy or nursing portion through extended health benefits, and third-party financing is available.

The core program is either 6 or 9 dosing sessions, each lasting 2 to 2.5 hours in the clinic with your therapist present. The 9-session option adds 2 integration sessions of 50 minutes, which can be in person or virtual. After the core sessions, you and the team decide whether ongoing therapy or maintenance care makes sense.

faqs.q: Who is eligible, and do I need a referral?
faqs.a: Eligibility is always decided in a medical consultation with a nurse practitioner, who reviews your health and mental health history. The clinic says the treatment may not suit people who are pregnant, have a personal history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled high blood pressure, a severe recent head injury or an allergy to the medicine. You can book the free discovery call yourself, and doctors can also send a referral through the clinic's form or the Ocean eReferral network.

faqs.q: What conditions does the Toronto clinic treat?
faqs.a: Field Trip Health Toronto works mainly with depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, substance use and chronic pain, usually in people for whom standard medication or talk therapy has not given enough relief. Its therapists also see clients for concerns such as grief, ADHD, eating disorders, bipolar disorder and trauma, including PTSD in veterans and first responders. Psychedelic therapy is offered as one part of a broader treatment plan, and results vary from person to person.

faqs.q: Where is Field Trip Health Toronto and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The clinic is at 30 Duncan Street, Suite 400, Toronto (M5V 2C3), near King and Queen Street West. It is a five-minute walk from Osgoode and St Andrew subway stations and about 15 minutes on foot from Union Station. Paid parking is nearby at 211 Adelaide Street West, but you cannot drive after a dosing session, so plan a ride home. The entrance has a five-step stair down to the elevator, so the clinic is not wheelchair accessible.

faqs.q: How long does a typical ketamine-assisted therapy session last?
faqs.a: Each session typically lasts around 2 to 2.5 hours.

faqs.q: Is ketamine-assisted therapy covered by insurance?
faqs.a: Ketamine-assisted therapy is not covered by public health plans, but many clients can use psychotherapy or nursing benefits toward part of the cost, and Field Trip Health Toronto offers third-party financing.

faqs.q: Can I continue taking my current medication while undergoing therapy at Field Trip Health Toronto?
faqs.a: It is important to consult with your medical provider before discontinuing any medication. Your care team will review your medications during the consultation; many people continue antidepressants during treatment, while others may need adjustments.

faqs.q: Do I have to live in the Toronto area to receive treatment at Field Trip Health Toronto?
faqs.a: No, Field Trip Health has clinics in several Canadian cities, including Ottawa, Hamilton, Kitchener-Waterloo, Thunder Bay, Sault Ste. Marie, Vancouver and Montreal, and an at-home program in some areas.

faqs.q: Are there any side effects of ketamine-assisted therapy?
faqs.a: Common side effects include mild dissociation, dizziness, and nausea, which typically subside within a few hours after the therapy session.
